Neither record carries any restraint markers (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so the duplication is actionable. The idiomatic Swift approach for cross-platform UIKit/AppKit divergence is a `#if canImport` conditional or a shared helper, not two separately maintained computed properties.

Both `uiColor` (line 53) and `nsColor` (line 63) in `Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift` would then delegate to this helper, differing only in the final platform type constructor (`UIColor` vs `NSColor`). Alternatively, use a `#if canImport(UIKit) / #if canImport(AppKit)` conditional compilation block with a single `color` computed property that resolves to the correct platform type, eliminating the need for two separate properties entirely.

A pure `generic-parameterization` does not fit because the type parameter would be constrained to a closed set of two platform types and the call sites select by name rather than by type inference. A `default-implementation` does not fit because there is no protocol involved. An `extract-to-common` does not fit because both properties already live in the same file and package. The most idiomatic Swift resolution is either a shared private helper or a platform-conditional single `color` property, neither of which maps cleanly to the named categories.
